faq: How does the approval request look?
A short message states what the agent wants to do, why, and shows a preview, for example the email text or refund amount. You tap approve, reject or edit, without logging in to anything new.
By default the action does not happen. The Standard and Premium packages send reminders and can pass the request to a backup person, so work does not stall for long.
Can small actions be approved automatically?
Yes, in the Premium package. You set a rule such as refunds under a set amount, and the agent proceeds alone while larger ones wait for a person.
Does this slow the work down?
A little, by design. Many teams only require approval for the few risky actions, so routine steps still run on their own and approvals take seconds each.

desc:
Human approval steps for AI agent actions let a person sign off on refunds, customer emails and price changes before they happen. Ecom Swift LLC builds the approve or reject step into your agent, with a clear preview and a saved record of every decision.

## What is a human approval step for an AI agent?

A human approval step is a pause built into an agent's workflow. The agent prepares an action, sends a short request to a named person, and waits. Nothing happens until that person approves, edits or rejects it.

The request carries the reason, the exact content the agent wants to send or change, and two buttons. It can arrive by email, in Slack or Teams, or on a simple web page. Once a decision is made, the agent either carries on or drops the action, and the decision is stored.

## Why risky actions need a person in the loop

An agent can be right nine times and wrong on the tenth. If the tenth mistake is a refund sent to the wrong order, an email with the wrong tone, or a price typed with a missing digit, the cost lands on your business and your customer. Models also misread unusual cases, and they do not feel the weight of a message that goes out under your name.

Approval steps limit that damage without removing the benefit. The agent still does the slow work: reading the request, gathering facts and drafting the result. The person only spends a few seconds on the final yes or no. Trust can then be built on evidence before the agent is given more freedom.

## How approval steps affect time, risk and trust

Reviewing a prepared draft takes far less effort than creating one, so you keep most of the time savings. The rare bad output is caught at the one point where it can still be stopped.

Approval also builds a record. When every decision is saved with a time and the approver's name, you can answer questions later about who allowed what.

## What a good approval workflow includes

- A request that states what the agent wants to do and why, in plain words.
- A preview of the exact email, refund, record change or message.
- Approve and reject buttons that work from a phone.
- An edit option, so the approver can fix a draft instead of rejecting it.
- A named approver for each action type, with a backup when that person is away.
- A reminder if nobody answers, and a safe default such as doing nothing.
- A rule to approve small actions automatically, such as anything under a limit you set.
- A saved record of each decision with a time stamp.

## What we do

We start by listing the actions your agent can take and sorting them by risk. Sending a thank-you note is low risk. Issuing a refund, changing a price or contacting a new customer is not. You decide which actions need a person and who that person is.

Next we build the approval step into your existing agent, using the channel your team already reads. We write the request template so that the approver sees what matters first. We connect the buttons to the agent so an approval resumes the work and a rejection stops it. Then we test every path: approve, reject, edit, no reply and the backup approver. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many action types, channels and audit features are covered.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Put approval on actions that cannot be undone or that reach a customer.
- Keep each request short enough to read in under a minute.
- Name one accountable approver per action type.
- Decide in advance what happens when no one replies.
- Review the saved decisions now and then and relax rules where the agent has proved reliable.

**Avoid:**
- Asking for approval on every small step, which trains people to click yes without reading.
- Sending requests to a shared inbox where no one feels responsible.
- Hiding the preview behind a link that needs a login.
- Letting the agent act after a long silence unless you chose that on purpose.
- Approving by reply to a message that does not show what was approved.

## Who this is for

This service suits a store owner whose agent drafts refund replies and who wants to confirm each one before it goes out. It suits an agency that lets an agent prepare client emails but needs an account manager to review the tone. It also suits a finance or operations lead who wants an agent to propose changes to prices or orders, with a record to show later.

## What we need from you

Tell us which actions need a person, who should approve each one, and where they prefer to receive requests. Give us access to the agent and to the email or chat tool as a collaborator, team member or developer user, wherever the platform supports it. We never need your passwords. We work in your own accounts, so the approval step and its records stay yours.
